raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a multi-series line chart showing ACC (%) as a function of Co-occurrence Number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale with major ticks at approximately 10, 100, and 1000, spanning from about 0 to a few thousand; four x positions are plotted (roughly ~5, ~30, ~300, and ~3000). The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging from about 38% to 66% with tick marks at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65. The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 38% at the smallest x to ~42% at the second point, then ~44% at the third and remaining near ~44% at the largest x. FT is a blue solid line with downward-triangle markers, rising from ~40% to ~43%, then ~46% and ~48% at the largest x. IKE is a red solid line with upward-triangle markers, increasing from ~43% to ~45%, then ~46.5% and ~49.5% at the largest x. MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, rising from ~44.5% to ~49%, then ~54% and ~56.5% at the largest x. MEMIT is a purple solid line with pentagon markers, increasing from ~44% to ~51%, then ~53% and ~55% at the largest x. ROME is a green solid line with square markers, increasing from ~51% to ~57%, then ~62.5% and ~66% at the largest x.
